title: Alabama's 4th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: Alabama's 4th Congressional District covers much of north-central and northwestern Alabama, including Cullman, Jasper, and parts of the Shoals area. Incumbent Republican Robert Aderholt, first elected in 1996, is seeking a 15th term in this heavily Republican district (Cook PVI: R+33). He will face Democratic nominee Amanda Pusczek, a registered nurse who won a competitive two-way primary on May 19, 2026. The race is not expected to be competitive; Aderholt's long incumbency and the district's strong Republican lean make him the overwhelming favorite in the general election.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of this writing. Alabama's 4th District is a safe Republican seat and has not been the subject of general-election polling.

candidates.name: Robert B. Aderholt
candidates.summary: Robert Aderholt is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Alabama's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 1996. He serves as Chairman of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health & Human Services, and Education, and is a member of the full Appropriations Committee. Before Congress, he served as Assistant Legal Advisor to Governor Fob James and as Municipal Judge for Haleyville, Alabama.

candidates.name: Amanda N. Pusczek
candidates.summary: Amanda Pusczek is a registered nurse and the Democratic nominee for U.S. House in Alabama's 4th Congressional District. She has over a decade of clinical nursing experience in hospitals, outpatient clinics, public schools, and correctional facilities, and served on the frontlines of the COVID-19 pandemic in New York City. Pusczek's campaign focuses on healthcare access, rural investment, and challenging corporate influence in politics.

forecast.rationale: No public opinion polls exist for this race, so the forecast is based entirely on district fundamentals and candidate context. Alabama's 4th Congressional District has a Cook PVI of R+33, making it one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country. Incumbent Robert Aderholt has held the seat since 1996 and is seeking a 15th term, providing a significant incumbency advantage. The Democratic nominee, Amanda Pusczek, won a competitive primary but faces structural headwinds in a district where Republican candidates routinely win by very large margins. While the complete absence of polling introduces some uncertainty, the district's extreme partisan lean, Aderholt's long tenure, and the race description all point to an overwhelming Republican advantage consistent with a safe Republican rating.
